A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 13-page VIB-Probe paper, including Appendices A and B. All material is readable. Pages 2-13 match exactly in extracted text and rendered images; page 1 differs only in affiliation, contact information, and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination detection, mitigation, transferability, robustness, and ablation experiments in Section 4, Tables 1-5, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original empirical results in Section 4, Tables 1-5, and Figure 3.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same attention-head feature extraction, VIB detector, BCE-plus-KL objective, and gradient-based inference-time head suppression. Appendix B's architecture is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate POPE's three subsets, AMBER, M-HalDetect, and COCO-Caption. The cross-task, cross-distribution, and image-perturbation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding experiments. Table 1 retains AvgEnt, AvgProb, RepProbing, MetaToken, and DHCP; Table 3 retains Vanilla, BeamSearch, PAI, and VCD. Table 2 and Figure 3 also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same base models, sample counts, splits, preprocessing, and evaluation procedures. Detection AUROC/AUPRC and mitigation accuracy, F1, and CHAIR metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: The transferability analysis in Figure 3, image-perturbation robustness experiment in Table 2, and KL-loss and layer-selection ablations in Tables 4-5 are identical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Statistical and uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1-5 and the result plots in Figures 1 and 3 retain all values and findings. For example, Table 1 reports the same VIB-Probe average POPE AUROC/AUPRC of 95.92/95.56 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Section 3, including Equations (1)-(14), are unchanged. The baseline and metric formulas in Appendices A and B are also identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about VIB-based detection, inference-time mitigation, state-of-the-art performance, robustness, and generalization.

C2.justification: Sections 4.2-4.4 retain the same interpretations of transferability, robustness, and ablation results. The limitations concerning standard attention architectures and required white-box access are unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameters, architecture, data preparation instructions, and mitigation settings in Section 4 and Appendices A-B are unchanged. Both abstracts retain the same promise of future public code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2, the research positioning elsewhere in the paper, and the reference list are unchanged. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: The first-page affiliation changes from School of Computer Science to College of Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence. The email line adds frzhang25, corrects a missing @, and reorders existing addresses; the arXiv stamp is updated. The scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-3, Tables 1-5, captions, and page organization are unchanged. The first-page metadata edits preserve the existing header structure; pages 2-13 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 updates affiliation and contact metadata, including correcting an email address, but leaves the scientific text, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged. These small editorial corrections produce no meaningful overall difference in paper quality.
